title: Fixed-error parallel Stein lemma for quantum channels

source.latex:
Fang, Gour, and Wang prove the weak channel Stein lemma and identify the
fixed-error, equivalently strong-converse-threshold, extension as unresolved
for general channel pairs \sourcecite{ref:p46-fang-gour-wang}{FGW25}.

items.latex:
The weak channel Stein lemma proves
  \begin{equation}
    \lim_{\delta\downarrow0}\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac1n
    D_{H,{\rm ch}}^\delta
    (\mathcal N^{\otimes n}\|\mathcal M^{\otimes n})
    =D_{\rm ch}^{\infty}(\mathcal N\|\mathcal M).
    \label{eq:p46-weak-stein}
  \end{equation}
  Equation~\eqref{eq:p46-weak-stein} yields the required lower bound at
  every fixed error, but not the converse inequality
  \sourcecite{ref:p46-fang-gour-wang}{FGW25}.

The equality in Eq.~\eqref{eq:p46-fixed-error-stein} is known when
  $\mathcal M$ is a replacer channel
  \sourcecite{ref:p46-cooney-mosonyi-wilde}{CMW16}.  It is also known for
  suitable pairs of idempotent channels that share a full-rank invariant
  state; this structured result explicitly leaves the general channel case
  open \sourcecite{ref:p46-singh-bergh}{SB26}.

comment.latex:
The question concerns parallel tests with an arbitrary entangled input across
the channel uses.  The weak-error result and the known structured channel
families do not establish Eq.~\eqref{eq:p46-fixed-error-stein} for an arbitrary
finite-dimensional pair $\mathcal N,\mathcal M$.
